entities.summary:
Lothar von Hochstaden was Bishop of Liège and archchancellor from 1157 until his death in 1194. He played a crucial role in the politics of the Holy Roman Empire, serving as a mediator between the Emperor and the nobility.

Von Hochstaden's tenure was marked by significant events, including the establishment of the Duchy of Limburg in 1167 and the signing of the Treaty of Strasbourg in 1179, which secured trade agreements with the Hanseatic League. His diplomatic efforts helped to maintain stability in a region fraught with conflict.

The legacy of Lothar von Hochstaden can be seen in the continued influence of the Bishopric of Liège throughout the Middle Ages. His leadership during this period played a key role in shaping the political and economic landscape of Western Europe.

In his later years, von Hochstaden was known for his commitment to the rebuilding of the cathedral at Liège, which had been damaged during the Investiture Controversy. This endeavor not only showcased his piety but also demonstrated his dedication to the spiritual well-being of his flock.

Today, Lothar von Hochstaden is remembered as a shrewd politician and a devoted servant of the Church. His diplomatic prowess and commitment to the welfare of his people have left an indelible mark on the history of the Holy Roman Empire.
